title: M53, NGC 5024
caption: The globular cluster M53, imaged by the KPNO 0.9-meter telescope

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This composite shows M53, also cataloged as NGC 5024, a globular cluster in the constellation Coma Berenices. The field is 14.7 arcminutes across.
M53 is an outlying globular cluster, lying about 60000 light-years from us and roughly the same distance from the center of our Galaxy.

A globular cluster is a dense, roughly spherical swarm of old stars held together by gravity. Our Galaxy is surrounded by many of them, some close to its center and others, like M53, far out in its outskirts. Because their stars formed together long ago, globular clusters act as fossils of the Milky Way's early history, and those at great distances help astronomers map the extended halo of stars that surrounds our Galaxy. The stars crowd most tightly toward the center of the cluster, while fainter members thin out toward the edges. Comparing stars within one cluster shows how stars of different masses age.
scale: M53 is about 60000 light-years away, according to NOIRLab.

understand.summary: The 0.9-meter telescope at Kitt Peak recorded M53 in visible light, and the images were combined into a composite. The filters and color mapping are not published.
understand.eye: The camera's exposures gather far more light than the eye, resolving many of the cluster's stars.
